key_insight: Shock strength and surface-asperity curvature strongly govern HMX jet velocity, temperature, and morphology, with coherent jets and molecular plumes linked to melting and vaporization, respectively.
engineering_relevance: Understanding asperity-driven jetting can help assess potential hot spot formation mechanisms in HMX-based explosives under shock loading.
method: All-atom nonreactive molecular dynamics of shock-loaded sinusoidal HMX surface asperities.
Varied shock strength, asperity geometry, system size, and crystallographic orientation.
Compared jet morphology with the ambient-pressure HMX phase diagram.
evidence_signal: Simulations spanning approximately 4–47 GPa found strong effects of shock strength and asperity curvature, but more modest effects of feature size and crystal orientation.
watch_item: Nonreactive simulations do not capture chemical ignition, and the proposed phase-diagram connection requires testing in other materials.
paper_title: Shock-driven Jetting at HMX Crystal Surface Asperities
